question: After the ethnic cleansing of Nagorno-Karabakh perpetrated by Azerbaijan, the Aliyev regime has not ceased to use warmongering and maximalist rhetoric. For example, on 24 April 2024, the President of Azerbaijan not only bragged about the mass exodus of Armenians from Nagorno-Karabakh but also suggested that EU Mission in Armenia (EUMA) observers should be grateful to him for not harming them.

On July 22, at the second so-called ‘Global Media Forum’ in Shusha, Aliyev again asserted territorial claims against the sovereign territory of Armenia and strongly condemned the decision of the Council of the European Union to provide the first assistance measure in support of the Armenian armed forces under the European Peace Facility and open up dialogue on visa liberalisation with Armenia. 1.
Why is the EU hesitant to condemn the Aliyev regime for threatening to kill the EU civilian mission observers – European citizens – deployed in Armenia?
When is the EU going to react to such unacceptable behaviour and distance itself from a policy of appeasement towards a dictatorial state such as Azerbaijan?

When will the EU impose sanctions against the leadership of Azerbaijan, particularly Mr Aliyev’s entourage, for the ethnic cleansing perpetrated against the Armenians of Nagorno-Karabakh, systematic violations of basic human rights, unlawful arrest and the imprisonment of prominent politicians, activists and journalists?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.10.2024) The EU has made it clear that the allegations and criticism directed by Azerbaijan against the EU Mission in Armenia (EUMA) are not acceptable. It is an utmost priority that EU monitors can implement the mission’s mandate in full safety and free from any form of intimidation or pressure, and EU has underlined this to all concerned parties.

The EU continues to engage with both Armenia and Azerbaijan, including with a view to supporting the normalisation of their relations and a long-lasting peace. The EU continues to address all relevant issues with Azerbaijan, including as part of the regular Human Rights Dialogue as well as in bilateral contacts.

The EU has reacted publicly to the human rights situation in the country in recent months, and has called on Azerbaijan to release all those independent journalists, human rights defenders and political activists imprisoned for exercising their fundamental rights1. The EU continues to provide support2 to displaced Karabakh Armenians (EUR 38.4 million in humanitarian aid and budget support).

The EU calls upon Azerbaijan to ensure the rights of Karabakh Armenians, including their right to return to their homes without intimidation and discrimination. The EU Delegation in Baku is following the situation on the ground, including the situation of detainees, and is in close contact with the International Committee of the Red Cross. Any decision on imposing sanctions is for the Council to make in unanimity.
